speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your health history, could you please tell me your age and whether you have ever experienced any spontaneous fractures or broken bones?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing that detailed history. I need to check your blood pressure, as hypertension is a key feature of this condition, and I will also order an abdominal ultrasound to look for any adrenal masses. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Pressure REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of ambiguous genitalia and bone fragility, I suspect a steroidogenesis defect. REQUEST TEST: Serum_17_Hydroxyprogesterone REQUEST TEST: Serum_Testosterone

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone and testosterone, combined with your history of ambiguous genitalia and bone issues, strongly suggest Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia, likely due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. Let me check your electrolyte levels to assess for salt-wasting, which is critical for management. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Electrolytes

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal electrolytes, this points to the simple virilizing form of 21-hydroxylase deficiency rather than the salt-wasting type. The bone fragility is likely due to long-standing androgen excess interfering with bone maturation, or potentially concurrent osteopenia. I will request imaging to assess your bone density and adrenal morphology. REQUEST TEST: DEXA_SCAN REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal DEXA scan suggests the fractures were likely due to minor trauma rather than significant osteoporosis, which aligns with the diagnosis of simple virilizing 21-hydroxylase deficiency. DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency, simple virilizing form)
